snip.t: Infection (spontaneous bacterial peritonitis): Bacterial translocation from gut lumen during bleeding — Fever, abdominal pain, ascites — Increases mortality by 15 %; warrants prophylactic antibiotics

Precipitating factors: GI bleed, infection (spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, TB, malaria), electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia, alkalosis), constipation, excess dietary protein, sedatives (benzodiazepines, opioids), renal dysfunction
Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP): High prevalence of ascites and limited early presentation
